title: Multiplicativity and the Euler Product of Jordan's Totient $J_k$
description: Builds the multiplicative theory of Jordan's totient J_k on top of erdos-1000-oq-03-oq-01, which proved that the count C_k(n) = #{ k-tuples mod n jointly coprime to n } equals the Dirichlet-convolution closed form J_k = μ * pow k. That established what J_k is; this entry establishes its multiplicative structure — the heart of the classical theory. Proves, with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (no native_decide): J_k = μ * pow k is a multiplicative arithmetic function, so J_k(mn) = J_k(m)·J_k(n) for coprime m, n (it is the Dirichlet convolution of the two multiplicative functions μ and pow k); the closed form J_k(n) = ∑_{d∣n} μ(d)·(n/d)^k; the value on prime powers J_k(p^i) = p^{ki} − p^{k(i−1)} for prime p and i ≥ 1 (only the squarefree divisors 1 and p survive the Möbius weights); the integer Euler product J_k(n) = ∏_{p∣n} (p^{k·v_p} − p^{k·(v_p−1)}) over the prime factors of n; positivity J_k(n) > 0 for k ≥ 1, n ≥ 1 (J_k is a genuine totient); the Euler-totient recovery J_1 = φ via Möbius inversion of Gauss's ∑_{d∣n} φ(d) = n; and the real Euler product J_k(n) = n^k · ∏_{p∣n}(1 − p^{−k}), the familiar closed form. Everything rests on Mathlib's arithmetic-function multiplicativity infrastructure (IsMultiplicative.mul, multiplicative_factorization); no analysis beyond the final cast to ℝ.

meta.author: Classical theory of Jordan's totient (Camille Jordan, 1870); formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib
meta.assumptions: None. Fully verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (no native_decide). #print axioms confirms all headline theorems (jordan_apply, isMultiplicative_jordan, jordan_prime_pow, jordan_eq_prod_primeFactors, jordan_pos, jordan_one_apply, jordan_eq_mul_prod_primeFactors) depend only on the foundational propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. The development is the exact μ-analogue of Mathlib's σ_k theory (isMultiplicative_sigma := isMultiplicative_zeta.mul isMultiplicative_pow), with μ in place of ζ.

mathlibDependencies.description: The Dirichlet convolution of two multiplicative arithmetic functions is multiplicative. Applied to J_k = μ * pow k, giving multiplicativity of Jordan's totient from isMultiplicative_moebius and isMultiplicative_pow.natCast.
For a multiplicative f and n ≠ 0, f(n) = ∏ over the prime factorization of f at prime powers. Turns multiplicativity of J_k into the Euler product J_k(n) = ∏_{p∣n} J_k(p^{v_p}).
μ(p^k) = if k = 1 then -1 else 0 for prime p. Collapses the divisor sum over a prime power to its k = 0 and k = 1 terms, yielding J_k(p^i) = p^{ki} − p^{k(i−1)}.
Möbius inversion over an AddCommGroup. Inverts Gauss's ∑_{d∣n} φ(d) = n into φ(n) = ∑_{d∣n} μ(d)·(n/d), establishing the recovery J_1 = φ.
n = ∏_{p∣n} p^{v_p(n)} for n ≠ 0. Reassembles ∏_{p∣n} p^{k·v_p} = n^k in the real Euler product J_k(n) = n^k · ∏(1 − p^{−k}).
divisors(p^k) = (range (k+1)).map (p ^ ·). Reindexes the divisor sum for J_k(p^i) over the exponents 0..i.

originalContributions: `jordan k := μ * (pow k : ArithmeticFunction ℤ)`: Jordan's totient packaged as a Dirichlet convolution, the μ-analogue of Mathlib's σ_k = ζ * pow k.
`isMultiplicative_jordan`: J_k is multiplicative, obtained for free as the convolution of the multiplicative μ and pow k — so J_k(mn) = J_k(m)·J_k(n) for coprime m, n.
`jordan_apply`: the closed form J_k(n) = ∑_{d∣n} μ(d)·(n/d)^k, matching the combinatorial count of the parent entry erdos-1000-oq-03-oq-01.
`jordan_prime_pow`: J_k(p^i) = p^{ki} − p^{k(i−1)} for prime p, i ≥ 1, by peeling the only two surviving Möbius terms (divisors 1 and p) from the prime-power divisor sum.
`jordan_eq_prod_primeFactors`: the integer Euler product J_k(n) = ∏_{p∣n} (p^{k·v_p} − p^{k·(v_p−1)}), from multiplicativity and the prime-power value.
`jordan_pos`: J_k(n) > 0 for k ≥ 1, n ≥ 1 — each Euler factor is positive — confirming J_k is a genuine (positive) totient.
`jordan_one_apply`: J_1 = φ, recovering Euler's totient via Möbius inversion of Gauss's divisor sum.
`jordan_eq_mul_prod_primeFactors`: the real Euler product J_k(n) = n^k · ∏_{p∣n}(1 − (p^k)⁻¹), the classical closed form, by pulling n^k = ∏ p^{k·v_p} out of the integer product.
prerequisites: Dirichlet convolution of arithmetic functions and the fact that it preserves multiplicativity
The Möbius function μ and its values on prime powers
Evaluation of a multiplicative function via its prime factorization (Euler products)
Möbius inversion and Gauss's identity ∑_{d∣n} φ(d) = n
